objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of a machine learning-based vascular graft in reducing graft infection rates within the first 30 days post-implantation.
dependent_variables: Graft infection rate within the first 30 days post-implantation
baseline: Historical graft infection rate of 10% within the first 30 days post-implantation.
procedure: Recruit 1000 patients with a history of vascular graft infections for the study.
Implant the machine learning-based vascular graft in the femoral artery of each patient.
Monitor the patients for 30 days post-implantation and record graft infection rates.
Compare the graft infection rates to the historical rate and patient population demographics.
expected_result: A 40% reduction in graft infection rates within the first 30 days post-implantation.
falsification_condition: Graft infection rate within the first 30 days post-implantation is not significantly lower than the historical rate (p-value < 0.05).
sample_requirements: 1000 patients with a history of vascular graft infections, aged 18-80, with a mix of male and female participants.
safety_constraints: Ensure that the machine learning-based vascular graft does not cause any adverse reactions or complications in patients.
information_gain: Understanding the effectiveness of machine learning-based vascular grafts in reducing graft infection rates and identifying potential areas for improvement in the design and implementation of such grafts.
